  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council of the City of Avalon
  made findings pursuant to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue
  this practice, it is required, that the City Council determine that the COVID-19 state of
  emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City
  Council in deciding to continue to have teleconference meetings and that state or local
  officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in
  connection with COVID-1 9, and that as a result of the COVID-1 9 emergency, meeting in
  person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these
  findings must be made every thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these
  findings at its upcoming March 15, 2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists

  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result

4.  City Renewal of General Services Agreement with Los Angeles County
  The General Services Agreement (GSA) between the City of Avalon and County of Los
  Angeles will expire on June 30, 2022. To ensure continuation of services, City Staff
  recommend renewing the existing agreement for a five-year term beginning on July 1,
  2022.
  Recommended Action

  County for a five year term beginning on July 1, 2022.

5.  Senate Bill 619 Resolution Providing Notification of Intent to Comply with Senate Bill 1383
  to CalRecycle
  Senate Bill 619 (SB 619) was introduced into law on October 5, 2021 and provides relief
  for municipalities and other jurisdictions that mean to comply with Senate Bill 1383, but
  need more time for implementation. SB 619 requires entities to submit to CalRecycle a
  resolution adopted by City Council providing notification of intent to comply with SB 1383
  as well as an application that outlines the current areas of non-compliance. The filing
  deadline for this relief is March 1, 2022.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution to approve the application providing notification of intent to comply with
  Senate Bill 1383 and authorize Staff to submit the documents to CalRecycle.

6.  Appointment of Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference
  and General Assembly Delegate
  The Annual Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference and
  General Assembly will be held in Palm Springs, CA from May 5-6, 2022. The City’s voting
  delegate will vote on agenda items pertaining to the General Assembly Business Meeting.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution appointing Mayor Ann H. Marshall as the City of Avalon voting delegate
  and appoint another member of the City Council as the alternate delegate for the Annual
  Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference and General
  Assembly in May 2022.

7.  First Reading of Zoning Ordinance Amendment ZOA 22-01, which Amends the Avalon
  Municipal Code to Regulate SB 9 Urban Lot Splits and Two-Unit Proiects and Finds the
  Ordinance to be Exempt from CEQA
  California legislature passed, and Governor Newsom signed into law, Senate Bill 9 (SB
  9”). SB 9 took effect on January 1, 2022 and requires the City to both: (1) allow any lot
  in a single-family residential zone to be split, roughly into halves, with resulting lots as
  small as 1,200 sf and (2) allow any lot in a single-family residential zone to be developed
  with up to two single-family primary dwellings. SB 9 requires the City to approve eligible
  lot splits and two-unit projects ministerially. SB 9 supplants local zoning ordinances and
  only allows cities to impose certain objective criteria for projects covered by SB 9. The
  proposed Zoning Ordinance incorporates the state mandated changes but also creates
  certain objective standards by which such projects may be considered.

  Recommended Action
  1. Find the Ordinance exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”)
  pursuant to: (1) Section 15358 of the CEQA Guidelines because it will not result in a direct
  or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment; (2) Section
  15061 (b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines as there is no possibility that this activity will have a
  significant adverse effect on the environment; and (3) Government Code sections
  65852.21(j) and 66411.7(n), which provide that adoption of an ordinance implementing
  the provisions of Government Code sections 66411.7 and 65852.21 (i.e., SB 9) is
  statutorily exempt from CEQA. 2. Introduce and waive all further readings of an ordinance
  of the City of Avalon amending the Avalon Municipal Code to add Section 9-2.10 and
  Article 7 to Chapter 9-5 regarding SB 9 urban lot splits and two- unit projects.

8.  First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Chapter 9-1.01 of Title 9, Planning and Zoning,
  of the Avalon Municipal Code Relating to Planning Commission Membership
  It was brought to City Staff’s attention that the Avàlon Municipal Code (AMC) does not
  require a member of the Planning Commission to be a full-time resident of Avalon. The
  current ordinance allows persons who own a business or serve in a management function
  to serve on the Planning Commission, regardless of their residency.
  Recommended Action
  Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending Chapter
  9-1.01 of Title 9, Planning and Zoning, of the Avalon Municipal Code Relating to Planning
  Commission Membership.

9.  Fourth of July Fireworks Vendor
  City Staff solicited quotes from various fireworks vendors and received two proposals  —

  one from Pyro Spectaculars for $35,000 and one from Garden State Fireworks, Inc. for
  $38,000. Both vendors are licensed and in good standing with the State. As per a
  longstanding agreement, Love Catalina traditionally pays for the firework show and has
  agreed to fund the show the City Council chooses.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with Garden State Fireworks, Inc.
  to provide the firework show on the Fourth of July.

10.  Award Contract for Joe Machado Field (JMF) Concession Stand
  On December 7, 2022 City Council authorized City Staff to issue a request for proposals
  (RFP) for the concessions at Joe Machado Field (JMF). The City received two proposals
  — one from Francisco Rojo and the other from Don Tony’s Fruit.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Francisco Rojo
  for the operations at the snack bar concession at Joe Machado Field and that the City
  Council waive any irregularities in the proposal.

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): At the February 1, 2022 City Council meeting, the City Council
of the City of Avalon (‘City’) made findings pursuant to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet
remotely. To continue this practice, it is required, that the City Council determine that the COVID
19 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the
City Council in deciding to continue to have teleconference meetings and that state or local
officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection
with COVID-19, and that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would
present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be
made every thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming
March 15, 2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in ED N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required under AR 361

Under AB 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social

  2. The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the
public, and the Governor’s declaration of a COVID-19 emergency still exists. Although vaccines

remain susceptible to infection. The disease can still spread rapidly through person-to-person

present in the State and County, the most predominant of which is the Delta variant. The City’s
economy is dependent upon visitors to the island, the presence of which, increases the likelihood
of transmission of the disease. Also, having members of the public attend council meetings at
locations where council members are in attendance due to their desire to avoid exposure to
COVID-1 9 poses an imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

Re-Authorization is Required Within 30 Days

The City Council made the findings listed above at its February 1, 2022 City Council meeting.
Consistent with the provisions of Government Code Section 54953(e), the findings must be made
every 30 days ‘after teleconferencing for the first time” under AB 361. Thus! if the City Council
desires to continue to meet remotely without having to post the location of each teleconference
location, the City Council must again find that the COVID-19 emergency still exists and that one
of the two following findings can be made: that state or local officials have imposed or
recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, or, that a
result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
or safety of attendees.

It is recommended that the City Council make these findings.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City Council will
have to follow the Brown Act provisions that existed prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: That the City Council make the findings under AB 361 at its March 15,
2022 City Council meeting.

SUBJECT:  City Renewal of General Services Agreement with Los Angeles

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to execute a General Services
Agreement with Los Angeles County for a five year term beginning on July 1 2022.

REPORT SUMMARY: The General Services Agreement (GSA) between the City of Avalon and
County of Los Angeles will expire on June 30, 2022. To ensure continuation of services, City
Staff recommend renewing the existing agreement for a five-year term beginning on July 1, 2022.

The GSA authorizes the County to provide services requested by the City. Services provided
under the GSA consist of “as-needed” time-limited services such as predatory animal control,
prosecution of city ordinances, direct assessment collection, and a variety of public works
services. Ongoing services such as law enforcement, LA County Fire/Lifeguards, or public health
code enforcement are provided by the applicable County departments through Special Services
Agreements. Any existing Special Services Agreement between the City and County are not
affected by renewal of this GSA.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have
an agreement with Los Angeles County to perform general services including direct assessment
collection.

SUBJECT:  Senate Bill 619 Resolution Providing Notification of Intent to Comply
  with Senate Bill 1363 to CalRecycle

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adapt a resolution to approve the application providing
notification of intent to comply with Senate Bill 1383 and authorize Staff to submit the documents
to CalRecycle.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City Council adopted an ordinance amending Title 6, Chapter 6-2 of
the Avalon Municipal Code relating to solid waste collection and organic waste disposal
reduction requirements as required by Senate Bill 1383 (SB 1383) on December 7, 2021.

58 1383 establishes targets to achieve a 50 percent reduction in the level of the statewide
disposal of organic waste from the 2014 level by 2020 and a 75 percent reduction by 2025. In
addition, not less than 20 percent of currently disposed edible food must be recovered for human
consumption.

The law also grants CalRecycle, the regulatory authority to achieve the organic waste disposal
reduction targets, including the ability to adopt regulations to implement these requirements.
CalRecycle adopted regulations in late 2020, which include the ability to enforce regulations.
CalRecycle’s actions may include conducting more frequent inspections, taking over direct
enforcement on non-compliant businesses within the City, establishing a schedule for City
compliance and a probationary period (requiring a work plan and that the jurisdiction
demonstrates it has sufficient staffing to implement the requirements of the law), and/or seeking
administrative penalties against the City of up to $10,000 per day.

On January 18, 2022, the City Council authorized the City Manager to execute the
amendment to the Franchise and Lease Agreement with CR&R to expand their services in
accordance with implementation of SB 1383. At the time the amendment was approved by the
City Council, City Staff and CR&R were working cooperatively to submit a Low Population
Wavier to CalRecycle that would alleviate some of the requirements associated with organic
waste collection as required by SB 1383.

Per City Council direction, CR&R’s timeline for the mobilization regarding implementing the SB
1383 regulations was extended to December 31, 2022 so the City had more time to determine
if its Low Population waiver would be approved by CalRecycle.
 On February 18, 2022 the City and CR&R submitted a Low Population Waiver to CalRecycle. At
the time this report was authored the City had not yet received confirmation if the waiver was
approved.

Senate Bill 619 (SB 619) was introduced into law on October 5, 2021 and provides relief for
municipalities and other jurisdictions that mean to comply with SB 1383, but need more time for
implementation. SB 619 requires entities to submit to CalRecycle a resolution adopted by City
Council providing notification of intent to comply with SB 1383 as well as an application that
outlines the current areas of non-compliance. The filing deadline for this relief is March 1, 2022.
By submitting the proposed resolution and application, fines for any violations that occur during
the 2022 or 2023 calendar year may be forgiven.

City Staff recommend adopting a resolution and submitting an application to CalRecycle as
outlined in SB 619 as a cautionary measure to ensure the City will not be subject to fines if the
Low Population Waiver is not approved.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: City infrastructure and compliance with State regulations.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Administrative penalties against the City for noncompliance can reach up
to $10,000 per day.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: If the City’s Low
Population Waiver is not approved, the City may be out of compliance for enforcing SB 1383
and could be subject to enforcement actions by CalRecycle (the regulatory authority to achieve
the organic waste disposal reduction targets), including administrative penalties against the City

  the Avalon Municipal Code to add Section 9-2.10 and Article 7 to Chapter 9-5 regarding

REPORT SUMMARY: The California legislature recently passed, and Governor Newsom
signed into law, Senate Bill 9 (SB 9’). SB 9 took effect on January 1, 2022 and requires the
City to both: (1) allow any lot in a single-family residential zone to be split, roughly into halves,
with resulting lots as small as 1.200 sf and (2) allow any lot in a single-family residential zone
to be developed with up to two single-family primary dwellings. SB 9 requires the City to
approve eligible lot splits and two-unit projects ministerially (i.e., without discretionary review,
conditions, or a hearing). Property owners can also utilize both of SB 9’s provisions, meaning
that an SB 9 lot split may be followed with an SB 9 two-unit project on each of the two new
lots, resulting in four total dwellings on what was formerly one single-family residential lot  —

all with only ministerial approval.

SB 9 supplants local zoning ordinances and only allows cities to impose certain objective criteria
for projects covered by SB 9. The proposed Zoning Ordinance incorporates the state mandated
changes but also creates certain objective standards by which such projects may be
considered. Most important to the City, applicants for such units will generally not have to
process their developments through the Planning Commission. The proposed Zoning
Ordinance Amendment ZOA 22-01 (attached as Attachment 1 and referred to herein as the
“Ordinance”) implements SB 9 by adding Section 9-2.10 to the City’s Subdivision title (to
 address urban lot splits), and Article 7 to Chapter 9-5 of the City’s Zoning title (to address two-
unit projects). The Ordinance will apply in the LU (Low Density Residential and Low Intensity
Recreational) zone.

  OwnerlApplicant:  City of Avalon
  Location of Project:  City-wide: Applicable regulations in LD (Low Density
  Residential and Low Intensity Recreational)
  PC #:  2776 (approved Jan 19, 2022)

Discussion:

SB 9 allows cities to impose objective zoning, subdivision, and design standards (collectively
 objective development standards”) on covered lot splits and two-unit projects. An objective
standard is a regulation that does not involve personal or subjective judgment and that is
verifiable by reference to an external and uniform benchmark or criterion (e.g., a height limit).

Generally, the proposed Ordinance is written to allow the City to exercise as much local control
over SB 9 projects as state law allows. Among other things, the Ordinance includes regulations
governing the following:

  •  Location (LU [Low Density Residential and Low Intensity Recreational] zones; not in
  sensitive, dangerous, historic areas; not on rental property (within last 3 years))
  •  Lot Size (2,400 Sf mm to split; 1.200 sf mm for resulting)
  •  Lot Access (adjoin ROW)
  •  Unit Size (800 sf max / du)
  •  Setbacks (normal, except as necessary to allow two units at 800 sf each; but no less
  than 4 feet side and rear)
  •  Use (residential-only, no short-term rental)
  •  Parking (one space, unless exempt by statute)
  •  Owner occupancy (three-year minimum on urban splits; permanent on two-unit projects)
  •  Architecture (must match other dwelling or dwellings on property; no direct lines of sight)
  •  Landscaping (limits on tree removal: required screening)
  •  Utilities (direct connections to service providers; all underground)
  •  Separate Conveyance Within a Lot (prohibited: no condos, no timeshares or separate-
  use co-ownerships)
  •  Deed Restriction (required; no short-term rental, non-residential use, or separate
  conveyance; development limited to SB 9 projects)

If the Council does not adopt the Ordinance, then the City would be limited to applying the State
mandates and the City’s existing objective development standards  —which did not anticipate
and were not enacted with ministerially-approved lot splits and two-unit projects in mind.
Approving such projects based solely on the States mandates and the City’s existing standards
would, among other things, threaten the character of existing neighborhoods and negatively
impact property values, personal privacy, and fire safety as many of the City standards would
be supplanted by the State’s mandates.

As noted above, the proposed Ordinance retains as much local control as possible under these
new State imposed mandates. Examples include the following:
   •  SB 9 does not contain standards governing architecture, landscaping, or fire hazard
  mitigation measures. The Ordinance imposes City-specific architecture, landscaping,
  and fire hazard mitigation measures on SB 9 projects in the City. 1

  •  SB 9 does not specifically regulate height; any height limit must be imposed by the local
  agency. The Ordinance provides that new SB 9-mandated primary dwelling units are
  subject to the LD zone’s height restrictions (LD zones are the only areas where SB 9
  projects are allowed in the City). 2

  •  SB 9 generally allows—but does not require—local agencies to impose their standard
  setback requirements on SB 9 projects. The Ordinance imposes the LD zone’s setback
  requirements on SB 9 projects, subject only to the limited instances where SB 9 requires
  otherwise.

The California legislature recently passed, and Governor Newsom signed into law, Senate Bill 9
(“SB 9”). SB 9 took effect on January 1, 2022 and requires the City to both: (1) allow any lot in
a single-family residential zone to be split, roughly into halves, with resulting lots as small as
1,200 sf and (2) allow any lot in a single-family residential zone to be developed with up to two
single-family primary dwellings. SB 9 requires the City to approve eligible lot splits and two-unit
projects ministerially (i.e., without discretionary review-, conditions, or a hearing). Property
owners can also utilize both of SB 9’s provisions, meaning that an SB 9 lot split may be followed
with an SB 9 two-unit project on each of the two new lots, resulting in four total dwellings on
what was formerly one single-family residential lot  —  all with only ministerial approval.
 DISCUSSION

SB 9 allows cities to impose objective zoning, subdivision, and design standards (collectively
“objective development standards”) on covered lot splits and two-unit projects. An objective
standard is a regulation that does not involve personal or subjective judgment and that is verifiable
by reference to an external and uniform benchmark or criterion (e.g., a height limit).

Generally, the proposed ordinance is written to allow the city to exercise as much local control
over SB 9 projects as state law allows. Among other things. the ordinance includes regulations
governing the following:

  •  Location (LD [Low Density Residential and Low Intensity Recreational] zone; not in
  sensitive, dangerous, historic areas; not on rental properly (within last 3 ycars))
  •  Lot Size (2,400 sf mm to split; 1,200 sf mm for resulting)
  •  Lot Access (adjoin ROW)
  •  Unit Size (800 sfmax / du)
  •  Setbacks (normal, except as necessary to allow two units at 800 sf eachz bitt no less than
  4 feet side and rear)
  •  Use (residential-only, no short-term rental)
  •  Parking (one space, unless exempt by statute)
  •  Owner occupancy (three-year minimum on urban splits; penuanent on two-unit projects)
  •  Architecture (must match other dwelling or dwellings on property; no direct lines of sight)
  •  Landscaping (limits on tree removal; required screening)
  •  Utilities (direct connections to servicc providers; all underground)
  •  Separate Conveyance Within a Lot (prohibited: no condos. no timeshares or separate-use
  co-ownerships)
  •  Deed Restriction (required; no short-term rental, non-residential use, or separate
  conveyance; development limited to SB 9 projects)

If the Council does not adopt the proposed ordinance, then the City would be limited to applying
the code’s existing objective development standards  which did not anticipate and were not
enacted with ministerially-approved lot splits and two-unit projects in mind. Approving such
projects based solely on the code’s existing standards would, among other things. threaten the
character of existing neighborhoods and negatively impact property values, personal privacy, and
fire safety.

REPORT SUMMARY: It was brought to City Staff’s attention that the Avalon Municipal Code
(AMC) does not require a member of the Planning Commission to be a full-time resident of
Avalon. The current ordinance allows persons who own a business or serve in a management
function to serve on the Planning Commission, regardless of their residency.

Specifically, AMC Chapter 9-1.01 provides:

A Planning Commission is hereby created which shall consist of seven members and one
alternate. Only those persons who are physically present in the City of Avalon or within two
miles of the City limits at least nine months of each calendar year (excluding special
circumstances such as extended personal or family illness, temporary absences necessitated
by the proposed appointee employment, military service, and similar situations) or who owns
or serves in a management position in an Avalon-based business. The members shall be
appointed by the Mayor with the approval of the Council. The tenure of any member of
the Planning Commission shall be terminable at any time by the Mayor upon the affirmative
vote of a majority of the entire Council.

In recent history, all Planning Commissioners have resided in Avalon full time during their term
on the Commission.

Utilizing ListServ, City Staff conducted a survey of other cities and their requirements for
Planning Commissioners. The following cities require planning commissioners to reside within
the city they serve:

Atwater  Clayton  Covina  Glendora
Bakersfield  Chula Vista  Del Mar  Irwindale
Beaumont  Coronado  Fort Bragg  Kerman
Brentwood  Costa Mesa  Fullerton  La Canada
 La Habra  Manhattan Beach  Rio Dell  Sonoma
La Verne  Napa  Sacramento  St. Helena
Laguna Beach  Newark  Santa Clara  Torrance
Lakeport  Orange  Santa Cruz  Upland
Lincoln  Oxnard  San Dimas  Vacaville
Livermore  Pleasant Hill  San Luis Obispo  Victorville
Lompoc  Pismo Beach  Signal Hill  Yorba Linda
Los Gatos  Redondo Beach  Solvang

The cities of Sonoma and Upland allows for non-residents to be appointed as Planning
Commissioners if approved by the City Council by a 4/5 vote. However, the City of Upland
noted that a non-resident has never been appointed to the Planning Commission.

Only the cities of Fortuna, Palm Springs and Shasta Lake responded as allowing for planning
commissioners to either reside in their cities or own a business within the City.

City Staff recommends eliminating the option of non-resident business owners or management
personnel to be able to serve on the Planning Commission.  The AMC Chapter 9-101 is
recommended to be amended to read as follows:

A Planning Commission is hereby created which shall consist of seven members and one
alternate. Only those persons who are physically present in the City of Avalon or within two
miles of the City limits at least nine months of each calendar year (excluding special
circumstances such as extended personal or family illness, temporary absences necessitated
by the proposed appointees employment, military service, and similar situations) may be
appointed to the commission. The members shall be appointed by the Mayor with the approval
of the Council. The tenure of any member of the Planning Commission shall be terminable at
any time by the Mayor upon the affirmative vote of a majority of the entire Council.

SUBJECT:  Fourth of July Fireworks Vendor

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with
Garden State Fireworks, Inc. to provide the firework show on the Fourth of July.

REPORT SUMMARY: Annually the City of Avalon provides a fireworks show as a part of the
Fourth of July schedule of events.

City Staff solicited quotes from various fireworks vendors and received two proposals one —

from Pyro Spectaculars for $35,000 and one from Garden State Fireworks, Inc. for $38,000.
Both vendors are licensed and in good standing with the State.

After an analysis of the two proposals, Staff recommends contracting Garden State Firework
Inc. Though the cost is $3,000 more, the proposal provides a substantially larger firework
show.

Comparatively, Pyro Spectaculars shoots 441 shells ranging from 3-8”. Garden State
Firework Inc. will shoot 2,310 shells ranging from 1-6” plus 6,500 assorted effects, equaling
8810 items shot in the air during an 18 minute show.

Staff vetted Garden State Firework, Inc. noted they are one of the oldest fireworks companies
in the United States with approximately 141 years in operation. Recent fireworks shows of
note include the 2020 Presidential Inauguration, Washington D.C. Fourth of July at the
National Mall, MLS All-Star and MLS Cup, Statue of Liberty Bicentennial Celebration, and Walt
Disney World, FL.

As per a longstanding agreement, Love Catalina traditionally pays for the firework show and
has agreed to fund the show the City Council chooses. The total budget for Fourth of July
events is $55,000. The barge accounts for $30,000 and the USC marching band is estimated
to cost $25,000, including transportation, lodging, and per diem. The cost for Fourth of July is
spread out over two fiscal years as many of the expenses are not paid until after July 1.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Enhance Recreational Opportunities.

FISCAL IMPACTS: No impact to the City’s budget. City contributes costs associated with the
barge, S30000, and USC marching band, $25,000, from the General Fund and Love Catalina
will pay for the fireworks.
 CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: City Staff will not
know how to proceed with regard to selecting a vendor for the Fourth of July fireworks display.

SUBJECT:  Award Contract for Joe Machado Field (JMF) Concession Stand

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an
agreement with Francisco Rojo for the operations at the snack bar concession at Joe Machado
Field and that the City Council waive any irregularities in the proposal.

REPORT SUMMARY; On December 7, 2022 City Council authorized City Staff to issue a
request for proposals (RFP) for the concessions at Joe Machado Field (JMF). The REP was
published on December 17, 2021. City Staff had a walk through schedule for January 3, 2022;
however, City Council requested the item come back for consideration before a walk through
was conducted. On January 4, 2022 City Council authorized Staff to continue with the RFP
process as approved on December 7, 2021. City Staff conducted a non-mandatory
walkthrough of the concession facility on January 18, 2022, two potential respondents
attended.

The original published deadline for the RFP was January 28, 2022 at 4:00 pm.; however, no
proposals were received by that time. The City issued an amendment to the RFP, extending
the deadline to February 17, 2022 at 4:00 pm. The City received two proposals one from
  —

Francisco Rojo and the other from Don Tony’s Fruit.

After an analysis of the proposals, City Staff determined neither proposal addressed all of the
requirements as outlined in the REP.

City Staff interviewed both respondents and assessed their proposals based on the best
interests of the City and the following criteria:

  1. Food/Menu.
  2. Experience. The qualifications and experience of business’s personnel who will be
  overseeing services and managing operations.
  3. MarketingNision. How the vendor plans to increase their market share for the future.
  4. Staffing.

Based on the two proposals and the grading criteria, Staff recommends awarding the contract
for JMF Concessions to Erancisco Rojo. (See attached criteria analysis)

Staff recommend City Council authorize the Community Services Supervisor and City Manager
to enter into negotiations with Francisco Rojo to establish the following terms for concession
operations:
   •  Continuous year-round operation of the concession stand.
  •  Require the concession stand to be open for all events at JMF, including recreational
  activities, school sports events, contracted league events, etc.
  •  Enter an approximate 33 month agreement with lessee, expiring on December 31
  2025, aligning the agreement with the other existing City agreements
  •  Before the initial term of operation is due, City Staff will conduct an internal review of
  operations. In the event both parties are satisfied and the Lessee is meeting the
  minimum requirements of the lease agreement allow for an additional 3-year term.
  •  Maintain insurance coverage consistent with the requirements outlined by the AMC.
  •  Comply with all aspects of the AMC, including the City’s Fats, Oil, Grease (‘FOG’)
  ordinance, Styrofoam, plastic straw and plastic bag ban ordinance, etc.
  •  Estabsh an initial lease rate of $2 per square foot for the first six months, and up to the
  first year of operations. After six months, the City Manager may consider an increase
  the lease rate to the standard $4 per square foot subject to annual CPI. The available
  lease space is comprised of 279 square feet of interior space and 121 square feet of
  outdoor space previously used to store a food vendor cart. The initial monthly rental
  rate of just the interior space is approximately $558 and $1,116 after six months of
  operation. Including the outdoor storage space, the initial monthly lease rate would be
  $800 and $1600 after six months of operation.

GOAL ALIGNMENT; Provide food service at Joe Machado Field for community gatherings
including but not limited to: City recreation and school athletic games; community special
events, and private gatherings were food is being served.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Lessee is responsible for a monthly rent amount of $1,116.00 or 8% of
gross receipts, or whichever is higher. This is for the concession stand only, if storage is added
for a vending cart rent would be $1,600/month.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Food services will not
be provided and no monthly rent be collected at Joe Machado Field for the snack bar services.

  PROPOSED SCOPE OF SERVICES

The City of Avalon presents this opportunity for interested individual and/or businesses to submit
proposals for the operation of the concession stand. It is the responsibility of the selected operator
to make any necessary tenant improvements to operate the concession on behalf of the City. The
operator shall have sole responsibility to finance and purchase all tenant improvements and
additional equipment. The concessionaire lease will take effect March 1, 2022.

The concession facility is intended for food and beverages. The concession area is 279 square
feet in size and is located adjacent to paved courtyard where seating may be placed at the
discretion of the concessionaire.

Concessions operations are a key component to the overall character of Joe Machado Field. The
selected proposer will be required to satisfy the following conditions as a part of the concession
operations;

Personnel

The operator will be responsible for hiring the necessary personnel to conduct the operation of
the concession standS The operator will comply with all federal! state and local laws related to
minimum wage! social security, nondiscrimination: unemployment compensation, and workers
compensationS Employees shall wear a uniform or other means of identification.

Operating Hours

Hours of operation may vary, based upon seasons and weather. Minimum hours would include.
but not be limited to all scheduled recreational and school game where attendance is greater than
30 persons, as well as all scheduled public and private events requesting food services. Operator
has first right of refusal for private events. Operator may choose to not open for team practices.

Off-Site Catering Opportunities

The facility may utilized for off-site catering opportunities. as such off-site catering does not impact
the operation of the concession stand for events at Joe Machado Field. If a conflict exists, the
lessee must immediately stop the off-site catering and service Joe Machado Field. All scheduling
of the facility: including concessionaire proposed hours of operation, shall be conducted through
the City of Avalon Community Services Department. The Community Services Department shall
maintain sole discretion as to approval.

Menu Items

The concessionaire is expected to serve quality food and beverages to meet the needs of the
visiting public. Simple menu items such as hot dogs, hamburgers, fries, and other snacks should
be offered at competitive prices. Beverages should include juices, water, and sodas. Beer and
wine sales are permitted on the condition the operator receives any required licensing including
ABC licensing to sell. The operations must comply with all aspects of the Avalon Municipal Code
(AMC), including the City’s Fats, Oil, Grease (FOG) ordinance, Styrofoam, plastic straw and
plastic bag ban ordinance.
